paragraphs: Park Aerospace Corp. ("Park"), and its subsidiaries (unless the context otherwise requires, Park and its subsidiaries are hereinafter called the "Company"), is an aerospace company which develops and manufactures solution and hot-melt advanced composite materials used to produce composite structures for the global aerospace markets. Park's advanced composite materials include film adhesives and lightning strike protection materials. Park offers an array of composite materials specifically designed for hand lay-up or automated fiber placement ("AFP") manufacturing applications. Park's advanced composite materials are used to produce primary and secondary structures for jet engines, large and regional transport aircraft, military aircraft, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles ("UAVs") commonly referred to as "drones"), business jets, general aviation aircraft and rotary wing aircraft. Park also offers specialty ablative materials for rocket motors and nozzles and specially designed materials for radome applications. As a complement to Park's advanced composite materials offering, Park designs and fabricates composite parts, structures and assemblies and low-volume tooling for the aerospace industry. Target markets for Park's composite parts and structures (which include Park's proprietary composite SigmaStrut™ and AlphaStrut™ product lines) are, among others, prototype and development aircraft, special mission aircraft, spares for legacy military and civilian aircraft and exotic spacecraft. Park's core capabilities are in the areas of polymer chemistry formulation and coating technology.
The Company's manufacturing and research and development facilities are located in Newton, Kansas.
Park was founded in 1954 by Jerry Shore, who was the Company's Chairman of the Board until July 14, 2004.

The Company makes available free of charge on its website, www.parkaerospace.com, its annual reports on Form 10-K, quarterly reports on Form 10-Q, current reports on Form 8-K and all amendments to those reports as soon as reasonably practicable after such material is electronically filed with or furnished to the Securities and Exchange Commission. None of the information on the Company's website shall be deemed to be a part of this Report.

AEROGLIDE®, AEROADHERE®, COREFIX®, ELECTROGLIDE®, ELECTROVEIL® and RADARWAVE® are registered trademarks of Park Aerospace Corp., and ALPHASTRUT®, PEELCOTE® and SIGMASTRUT® are common law trademarks of Park Aerospace Corp.

The Company designs, develops and manufactures engineered, advanced composite materials and advanced composite structures and assemblies and low-volume tooling for the aerospace markets and prototype tooling for such structures and assemblies.

The Company's aerospace composite materials are designed, developed and manufactured at its facility located at the Newton, Kansas Airport. The Company's aerospace composite structures and assemblies and low-volume tooling are also developed and manufactured at its facility located in Newton, Kansas.

Park offers a wide range of aerospace composite materials manufacturing capability, as well as composite structures design, assembly and production capability, all in its Newton facility. Park offers composite aircraft and space vehicle structures design and assembly services, in addition to "build-to-print" services. The Company believes that the ability to manufacture and develop both composite materials and structures at a single location can facilitate the needs of the aircraft and space vehicle industries.

The Company is planning to build a new composites material manufacturing and development facility to support expected significantly increased demand and future opportunities for the Company's commercial aircraft and defense-related businesses. The facility will be a fully functional and integrated plant that will include manufacturing and development activities. It will also include full production lab facilities, office space, storage and freezer space and ancillary equipment necessary to support all plan manufacturing operations. The site of this new location is currently being finalized and construction is expected to begin in fiscal year 2027.

Under a Business Partner Agreement with ArianeGroup SAS of Les Mureaux, France, Park is the exclusive North American distributor of ArianeGroup's RAYCARB C2B® NG proprietary product. RAYCARB C2B® NG is used to produce ablative composite materials for critical rocketry and missile systems. Park is a long-term customer of ArianeGroup and uses ArianeGroup's RAYCARB C2B® NG product in the production of many of Park's key ablative materials, which Park supplies into critical rocket and missile programs.

On March 27, 2025, Park and ArianeGroup entered into an agreement under which Park would advance funds to ArianeGroup against future purchases of C2B® product in the total amount in Euros of €4,587,000 payable in three installments in 2025, 2026, and 2027. These advanced funds are to be used to help fund the purchase and installation, by ArianeGroup, of additional manufacturing equipment for ArianeGroup's production of C2B® product.

The aerospace composite materials manufactured by the Company and its competitors are used primarily to fabricate light-weight, high-strength structures with specifically designed performance properties. Composite materials are typically highly specified combinations of resin formulations and reinforcements. Reinforcements can be unidirectional fibers, woven fabrics, or non-woven goods such as mats or felts. Resin formulations are typically highly proprietary and include various chemical and physical mixtures. The Company produces resin formulations using various epoxies, polyesters, phenolics, cyanate esters, polyimides and other complex matrices. The reinforcement combined with the resin is referred to as a "prepreg". Aerospace composite materials can be broadly categorized as either thermosets or thermoplastics. While both material types require the addition of heat to form a consolidated laminate, thermoplastics can be reformed using additional heat. Once fully cured, thermoset materials cannot be further reshaped. The Company believes that the demand for thermoset advanced materials is greater than that for thermoplastics due to the fact that parts fabrication processes for continuous fiber reinforced thermoplastics require much higher temperatures and pressures and are, therefore, typically more capital intensive than parts fabrication processes for most thermoset materials.

The Company works with aerospace Original Equipment Manufacturers ("OEMs"), such as general aviation aircraft manufacturers and commercial aircraft manufacturers, and certain tier 1 suppliers (manufacturers of major components or systems such as engines, control systems, landing gear, braking systems, flight deck, avionics, aerostructures, electronic warfare systems and interior cabin products that are supplied to the OEMs) to qualify its aerospace composite materials or structures and assemblies for use on current and upcoming programs. The Company's customers typically design and specify a material specifically to meet the requirements of the customer's application and processing methods. Such customers sometimes work with a supplier to develop the specific resin system and reinforcement combination to match the application. Composite structure fabrication methods may include hand lay-up, resin infusion or more advanced automated lay-up processes. Automated lay-up processes include automated tape lay-up, automated fiber placement and filament winding. These automated fabrication processes require different material formats but similar materials to hand lay-up. After the lay-up process is completed, the material is cured by the addition of heat and pressure. Cure and consolidation processes typically include vacuum bag/oven curing, high pressure autoclave and press forming. After the structure has been cured, final finishing and trimming, and assembly of the structure, is performed by the fabricator or the Company.

The aerospace composite materials products manufactured by the Company are primarily thermoset curing prepregs. The Company has developed proprietary resin formulations to suit the needs of the markets in which it participates by analyzing the needs of the markets and working with its customers. The complex process of developing resin formulations and selecting the proper reinforcement is accomplished through a collaborative effort of the Company's research and development, materials and process engineering and technical sales and marketing resources working with the customers' technical staff. The Company focuses on developing a thorough understanding of its customers' businesses, product lines, processes and technical challenges. The Company develops innovative solutions which utilize technologically advanced materials and concepts for its customers.

paragraphs: The business of the Company faces numerous risks, including those set forth below or those described elsewhere in this Form 10-K Annual Report or in the Company's other filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The risks described below are not the only risks that the Company faces, nor are they necessarily listed in order of significance. Other risks and uncertainties may also affect the Company's business. Any of these risks may have a material adverse effect on the Company's business, financial condition, results of operations or cash flow.

The Company's suppliers of raw material, supplies and equipment could be impacted by geopolitical events, such as the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, thus interrupting the Company's supply chain. Additionally, the Company's customers may experience interruptions from other suppliers that could cause a customer to delay or cancel orders. Other geopolitical risks include political and economic instability and disruptions, restrictions on the transfer of funds, trade conflicts and the imposition of duties, tariffs, and similar government charges, as well as import and export controls. Such risks could reduce demand for the Company's products and increase the Company's cost of operations, which could have a material adverse effect on the Company's business and results of operations.

The Company's operating results could be negatively affected if the Company were unable to maintain and increase its technological and manufacturing capability and expertise to develop new products on a timely basis. Although the Company believes that it has certain technological and other advantages over its competitors, maintaining such advantages will require the Company to continue investing in research and development and sales and marketing. There can be no assurance that the Company will be able to make the technological advances necessary to maintain such competitive advantages or that the Company can recover major research and development expenses.

Certain of the Company's principal competitors are substantially larger and have greater financial resources than the Company, and the Company's operating results will be affected by its ability to maintain its competitive positions in these industries. The aerospace composite materials and composite structures and assemblies industries are intensely competitive, and the Company competes worldwide in the markets for such products.

Changes in the cost of raw materials, supplies, labor, utilities or services could materially increase the Company's cost of operations. The Company is experiencing inflation in raw material and other costs. The impact of inflation on the Company's profits has been partially mitigated by the Company's ability to adjust pricing for a large portion of its sales to pass the impact of inflation through to its customers. Significant increases in the cost of materials, supplies, labor, utilities or services purchased by the Company could also materially increase the Company's cost of operations and could have a material adverse effect on the Company's business and results of operations if the Company were unable to pass such increases through to its customers.

There are a limited number of qualified suppliers of the principal materials used by the Company in its manufacture of aerospace composite materials and composite structures and assemblies. The Company has qualified alternate sources of supply for many, but not all, of its raw materials, but certain raw materials are produced by only one supplier. In some cases, substitutes for certain raw materials are not always readily available, and in the past, there have been shortages in the market for certain of these materials. Raw material substitutions for certain aircraft-related products may require governmental (such as FAA) approval. While the Company considers its relationships with its suppliers to be strong, a shortage of these materials or a disruption of the supply of these materials caused by a natural disaster or otherwise could materially increase the Company's cost of operations and could materially adversely affect the business and results of operations of the Company. Likewise, significant increases in the cost of materials purchased by the Company could also materially increase the Company's cost of operations and could have a material adverse effect on the Company's business and results of operations if the Company were unable to pass such increases through to its customers. If one or more of the Company's suppliers is required to temporarily close manufacturing facilities, the Company's ability to procure raw materials for its manufacturing processes may become limited and this could ultimately limit the Company's ability to manufacture its products.

paragraphs: MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS.

Park Aerospace Corp. ("Park" or the "Company") is an aerospace company which develops and manufactures solution and hot-melt advanced composite materials used to produce composite structures for the global aerospace markets. Park's advanced composite materials include film adhesives and lightning strike protection materials. Park offers an array of composite materials specifically designed for hand lay-up or automated fiber placement (AFP) manufacturing applications. Park's advanced composite materials are used to produce primary and secondary structures for jet engines, large and regional transport aircraft, military aircraft, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs commonly referred to as "drones"), business jets, general aviation aircraft and rotary wing aircraft. Park also offers specialty ablative materials for rocket motors and nozzles and specially designed materials for radome applications. As a complement to Park's advanced composite materials offering, Park designs and fabricates composite parts, structures and assemblies and low-volume tooling for the aerospace industry. Target markets for Park's composite parts and structures (which include Park's proprietary composite SigmaStrut™ and AlphaStrut™ product lines) are, among others, prototype and development aircraft, special mission aircraft, spares for legacy military and civilian aircraft and exotic spacecraft.

The Company's fiscal year is the 52- or 53-week period ending the Sunday nearest to the last day of February. The 2026, 2025, and 2024 fiscal years ended on March 1, 2026, March 2, 2025, and March 3, 2024, respectively. The 2026 and 2025 fiscal years each consisted of 52 weeks and the 2024 fiscal year consisted of 53 weeks. Unless otherwise indicated in this Discussion and Analysis, all references to years and quarters in this Discussion and Analysis are to the Company's fiscal years and fiscal quarters, and all annual and quarterly information in this Discussion and Analysis is for such fiscal years and quarters, respectively.

The Company's total net sales worldwide in 2026 were 18% higher than in 2025. The increase in sales was primarily driven by an increase in sales in the military and commercial aircraft markets and, to a lesser extent, higher sales in the space market, partially offset by lower sales in the Business Aircraft market.

The Company's gross profit margin, measured as a percentage of sales, increased to 30.9% in 2026 from 28.4% in 2025. The higher gross profit margin was the result of higher sales prices, a more favorable sales mix and lower labor and overhead costs as a percentage of sales due to improved leverage of these costs.

The Company's earnings from operations in 2026, as a percentage of sales, were 18.4% compared to 15.1% in 2025, primarily as a result of the higher sales and improved gross margin partially offset by higher selling, general and administrative expenses. The higher selling, general and administrative expenses were due to higher salaries and fringe benefits, travel expenses, professional fees, incentive compensation and research and development expenses in 2026. The Company's net earnings in 2026 were 92% higher than in 2025, primarily due to an 18% increase in sales, higher gross margins, higher interest income in 2026 and a $1.1 million storm damage charge in 2025. These increases were offset by higher selling, general and administrative expenses in 2026 as well as higher income tax expense in 2026. While income taxes increased in whole dollars in 2026, the 2026 tax rate decreased compared to the 2025 tax rate primarily as the result of a deferred tax provision recorded in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025 on unrepatriated foreign earnings partially offset by a higher benefit from the reduction in uncertain tax positions in 2025 as compared to 2026.

The Company continues to experience inflation in costs of raw materials and supplies, freight costs and other costs and expenses. The impact of inflation on the Company's profits has been partially mitigated by the Company's ability to adjust pricing for a large portion of its sales to pass the impact of inflation through to its customers. The Company also experienced increasing costs resulting from the imposition of duties, tariffs, and similar governmental charges by the United States and certain foreign jurisdictions on the products of its customers and suppliers. The impact of these tariffs and other duties was largely mitigated by the Company's ability to adjust pricing to pass the impact of these costs through to its customers.

Programs in which the Company participates as a supplier are, in some cases, experiencing supply chain issues from other suppliers to the programs that could result in delays in production for certain customers of the Company. These issues may be exacerbated by trade conflicts that restrict the transfer of funds or impose import and export controls on the Company's products or supply chain inputs. The Company's sales could also be impacted by these supply chain challenges to the extent that its customers are experiencing them from their other suppliers.

While the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East have had a negative impact on the Company's results of operations due to delayed shipments, the Company may experience an increase in future sales due to increases in spending worldwide on missile defense systems and other defense programs. The Company does not have any significant customers in Russia or Ukraine but does have customers in Israel. The Company has experienced some increases to raw material costs from overseas suppliers due to the impacts of the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East.

The Company has a number of long-term contracts pursuant to which certain of its customers, some of which represent a substantial portion of the Company's revenue, place orders. Long-term contracts with the Company's customers are primarily requirements based and do not guarantee quantities. An order forecast is generally agreed concurrently with pricing for any applicable long-term contract. This order forecast is then typically updated periodically during the term of the underlying contract. Purchase orders are generally received more than three months in advance of delivery.

paragraphs: Park Aerospace Corp. ("Park"), 以及其子公司（除非文意另有明確說明，Park 以及其子公司以下簡稱為 "本公司")，為一家航空業公司，從事開發與製造用以生產全球航空市場複合結構之解決方案與熱熔先進複合材料。Park 的先進複合材料包括薄膜黏合劑與雷擊保護材料。Park 提供一系列專為手工鋪層或自動纖維置放 ("AFP") 製造應用所設計之複合材料。Park 的先進複合材料用以生產噴射引擎、大型及區域運輸飛機、軍用飛機、無人機 ("UAVs") 常見稱為 "無人機"、商務飛機、一般航空飛機及旋翼飛機之主要與次要結構。Park 還提供專門用以火箭引擎與噴嘴之燒蝕性材料，以及為雷達罩應用特別設計之材料。為補強 Park 之先進複合材料產品線，Park 設計與製造航空業之複合零件、結構與組裝件及低產量模具。Park 複合零件與結構之目標市場（包括 Park 自有之複合 SigmaStrut™ 與 AlphaStrut™ 產品線）包括原型與開發飛機、特殊任務飛機、遺產軍用與民用飛機之備件及特殊太空飛行器。
本公司之製造與研究發展設施位於 Kansas 之 Newton 市。
Park 於 1954 年由 Jerry Shore 資助成立，Jerry Shore 為本公司董事長直至 2004 年 7 月 14 日。
本公司於其網站 www.parkaerospace.com 提供年度報告（10-K 表格）、季報（10-Q 表格）、現況報告（8-K 表格）以及所有對這些報告之修正案，於這些資料電子檔提交或提供給證券交易委員會後儘速免費提供。本公司網站上之資訊不應視為本報告之一部分。
AEROGLIDE®, AEROADHERE®, COREFIX®, ELECTROGLIDE®, ELECTROVEIL® 和 RADARWAVE® 為 Park Aerospace Corp. 之註冊商標，ALPHASTRUT®, PEELCOTE® 和 SIGMASTRUT® 為 Park Aerospace Corp. 之普通法商標。
本公司設計、開發與製造用以航空市場之工程先進複合材料、先進複合結構與組裝件及低產量模具，以及用以這些結構與組裝件之原型模具。
本公司之航空複合材料於位於 Kansas 之 Newton 市機場之設施中設計、開發與製造。本公司之航空複合結構與組裝件及低產量模具亦於位於 Kansas 之 Newton 市之設施中開發與製造。
Park 提供廣泛之航空複合材料製造能力，以及複合結構設計、組裝與生產能力，皆位於其 Newton 市設施中。Park 還提供複合飛機與太空飛行器結構設計與組裝服務，以及 "按圖施工" 服務。本公司認為，能在單一地點製造與開發複合材料與結構之能力，可協助航空與太空飛行器產業之需求。
本公司預計將興建一座新的複合材料製造與研發廠房，以支持預期顯著增加的 demand 以及未來的商機，用於本公司商業飛機與防禦相關業務。該廠房將為一座完全功能且整合的工廠，包含製造與研發活動。該廠房亦包含完整的生產實驗室設施、辦公空間、儲存與冷凍空間以及支援所有製造作業所需的輔助設備。此新廠址目前仍在最終確認中，預計於會計年度 2027 年開始動工。

根據與法國 Les Mureaux 的 ArianeGroup SAS 籤訂的商業夥伴協議，Park 為 ArianeGroup 的 RAYCARB C2B® NG 專屬產品在北美地區的經銷商。RAYCARB C2B® NG 用於製造關鍵火箭與飛彈系統的燒蝕複合材料。Park 為 ArianeGroup 的長期客戶，並使用 ArianeGroup 的 RAYCARB C2B® NG 產品製造許多 Park 的關鍵燒蝕材料，這些材料供應至關鍵火箭與飛彈計畫。
於 2025 年 3 月 27 日，Park 與 ArianeGroup 籤訂協議，Park 將預先提供資金給 ArianeGroup，以對應未來購買 C2B® 產品的總金額為 €4,587,000，分三期於 2025 年、2026 年及 2027 年支付。這些預先資金將用於協助 ArianeGroup 購買及安裝額外的製造設備，以生產 C2B® 產品。

本公司與競爭對手製造的航空複合材料主要用於製造輕量且高強度的結構，具備特定設計的性能特性。複合材料通常是高度指定的樹脂配方與增強材料組合。增強材料可以是單向纖維、織物或非織造材料，例如墊片或絨布。樹脂配方通常是高度專利的，包含各種化學與物理混合物。本公司使用各種環氧樹脂、聚酯、酚醛樹脂、氰酸酯、聚醯亞胺及其他複雜基質製造樹脂配方。增強材料與樹脂結合後稱為 "預浸料"。航空複合材料可大致分為熱固性或熱塑性兩類。雖然兩種材料類型都需要加熱以形成壓合層壓板，但熱塑性材料可以透過額外加熱重新塑形。一旦完全固化，熱固性材料無法再重新塑形。本公司認為熱固性先進材料的需求大於熱塑性材料，原因是連續纖維增強熱塑性材料的零件製造過程需要更高的溫度與壓力，因此通常比大多數熱固性材料的零件製造過程更具資本密集性。

本公司與航空業原廠製造商（"OEMs"），例如一般飛機製造商與商業飛機製造商，以及某些一級供應商（製造主要零組件或系統的廠商，例如引擎、控制系統、起落架、剎車系統、飛行甲板、航電系統、航空結構、電子戰系統及客艙產品，這些產品供應給 OEMs）合作，以驗證本公司航空複合材料或結構與組裝件用於現有與未來計畫。本公司客戶通常會設計並指定特定材料以符合客戶應用與製造方法的需求。這些客戶有時會與供應商合作，開發符合應用需求的特定樹脂系統與增強材料組合。複合結構製造方法可能包括手動鋪層、樹脂滲透或更先進的自動鋪層過程。自動鋪層過程包括自動帶材鋪層、自動纖維置放與纖維繞製。這些自動製造過程需要不同格式的材料，但與手動鋪層使用相似的材料。完成鋪層過程後，材料會透過加熱與壓力進行固化。固化與壓合過程通常包括真空袋/烤箱固化、高壓 autoclave 與壓製成型。結構固化後，會進行最終的修整與裁切，以及結構的組裝，由製造商或本公司執行。
本公司製造的航空複合材料產品主要為熱固性固化預浸料。本公司已透過分析市場需求並與客戶合作，開發專利樹脂配方以符合其參與市場的需求。開發樹脂配方與選擇適當增強材料的複雜過程，是由本公司研發、材料與製程工程及技術銷售與行銷資源與客戶技術團隊共同合作完成。本公司專注於深入瞭解客戶的業務、產品線、製造流程與技術挑戰。本公司開發創新解決方案，利用先進的材料與概念為客戶服務。

Park Aerospace Corp. ("Park" 或 "本公司") 為一家航空業公司，開發與製造用於全球航空市場生產複合結構之解決方案與熱熔先進複合材料。Park 的先進複合材料包括薄膜黏合劑與雷擊保護材料。Park 提供一系列複合材料，專門設計用於手工鋪層或自動纖維置放 (AFP) 製造應用。Park 的先進複合材料用於生產噴氣發動機、大型與區域運輸飛機、軍用飛機、無人機 (UAVs 常被稱為 "無人機" )、商務飛機、一般航空飛機與旋翼飛機之主要與次要結構。Park 還提供專用的燒蝕材料用於火箭引擎與噴嘴，以及專為雷達罩應用設計的特殊材料。作為對 Park 先進複合材料產品線的補充，Park 設計與製造複合零件、結構與組裝件及低產量模具，用於航空產業。Park 複合零件與結構 (包括 Park 自有複合 SigmaStrut™ 與 AlphaStrut™ 產品線) 的目標市場包括，但不限於原型與開發飛機、特殊任務飛機、遺產軍用與民用飛機零組件，以及特殊太空飛機。

本公司會計年度為 52 或 53 週的會計年度，於每年 2 月最後一天附近之週日結束。2026、2025 與 2024 會計年度分別於 2026 年 3 月 1 日、2025 年 3 月 2 日與 2024 年 3 月 3 日結束。2026 與 2025 會計年度各為 52 週，而 2024 會計年度為 53 週。除非本討論與分析另有說明，否則本討論與分析中所有提及年份與季度之參考皆為本公司會計年度與會計季度，且本討論與分析中所有年度與季度資訊皆為對應之會計年度與會計季度。
本公司 2026 年全球淨銷售額較 2025 年成長 18%。銷售額成長主要來自軍用與商用飛機市場銷售額增加，其次為太空市場銷售額增加，部分抵銷了商務飛機市場銷售額下降。
本公司 2026 年毛利率，以銷售額百分比計算，較 2025 年 28.4% 增加至 30.9%。較高的毛利率是因為銷售價格提高、銷售組合更為有利，以及勞動與間接費用佔銷售額百分比下降，因這些費用的 leverage 有所改善。

本公司營業收入在2026年的營業獲利率為銷售額的18.4%，較2025年的15.1%為高，主要係因銷售額增加及毛利率改善，部分抵銷營銷、一般及行政費用增加的影響。營銷、一般及行政費用增加係因2026年員工薪資及福利、差旅費用、專業費用、激勵報酬及研究發展費用增加所致。本公司2026年淨獲利較2025年成長92%，主要係因銷售額成長18%、毛利率提高、2026年利息收入增加以及2025年計提1.1百萬美元風災損壞費用所致。這些成長被2026年營銷、一般及行政費用增加以及2026年所得稅費用增加所抵銷。雖然2026年所得稅費用以整數美元計算增加，但2026年稅率較2025年稅率為低，主要係因財務會計年度2025年第四季計提遞延所得稅資產，針對未匯回的海外營業利潤，部分抵銷2025年較2026年所得稅資產減損的利潤所得稅減免效益。
本公司持續面臨原材料與供應品成本、運輸費用及其他成本與費用的通貨膨脹。通貨膨脹對本公司利潤的影響已部分被本公司調整價格以將通貨膨脹影響轉嫁給客戶的能力所緩解。本公司也因美國與某些外國司法管轄區對其客戶與供應商產品課徵關稅、稅收及類似政府費用而面臨成本增加。這些關稅及其他費用的影響已 largely 被本公司調整價格以將這些成本轉嫁給客戶的能力所緩解。
本公司參與的供應商計畫，在某些情況下，因其他供應商的供應鏈問題，可能導致某些客戶的生產延遲。這些問題可能因貿易衝突而惡化，限制資金轉移或對本公司產品或供應鏈投入課徵進出口管制。本公司銷售額也可能因這些供應鏈挑戰而受到影響，若其客戶因其他供應商而面臨相同問題。
雖然烏克蘭與中東地區的戰爭對本公司的營業成果造成負面影響，導致出貨延遲，但本公司可能因全球對飛彈防禦系統及其他防禦計畫的支出增加，而在未來看到銷售額的成長。本公司在俄羅斯或烏克蘭沒有任何重大客戶，但擁有以色列的客戶。本公司因烏克蘭與中東地區的戰爭影響，從海外供應商處經歷了一些原材料成本的增加。
本公司與若干客戶簽有長期合約，根據這些合約，部分客戶（其中一些客戶代表本公司營業收入的相當大一部分）下訂單。與本公司客戶簽訂的長期合約主要是基於需求，並不保證訂購數量。任何適用的長期合約的訂單預測通常會與價格同時協議。此訂單預測通常在合約期間內定期更新。訂單通常會在交貨前三個月以上收到。

paragraphs: 本公司業務面臨許多風險，包括下列所列風險或其他在本 Form 10-K 年度報告或本公司其他向證券交易委員會提交的申報文件中所描述的風險。下列所描述的風險並非本公司所面臨的唯一風險，也未必按重要性順序列出。其他風險與不確定性也可能影響本公司的業務。任何這些風險都可能對本公司的業務、財務狀況、營運結果或現金流造成重大不利影響。
本公司原料、物料及設備供應商可能受地緣政治事件影響，例如烏克蘭與中東戰爭，進而幹擾本公司的供應鏈。此外，本公司客戶可能因其他供應商的中斷而導致延遲或取消訂單。其他地緣政治風險包括政治與經濟不穩定、中斷與限制資金轉移、貿易衝突以及課徵關稅、稅收及其他類似政府費用，以及進出口管制。這些風險可能降低本公司產品的需求，並提高本公司的營運成本，進而對本公司業務與營運結果造成重大不利影響。
若本公司無法維持並提升其科技與製造能力及專業知識，以及時開發新產品，則本公司營運結果可能受到負面影響。雖然本公司認為其在某些科技及其他方面具有優勢於競爭對手，但要維持這些優勢，本公司必須持續投資於研究與開發及銷售與行銷。無法確保本公司能做出必要的科技進展以維持這些競爭優勢，或本公司能回收重大研究與開發費用。
本公司部分主要競爭對手規模遠較本公司為大，且擁有較多財務資源，因此本公司營運結果將受其維持在這些產業中競爭地位的能力影響。航空複合材料與複合結構及組裝產業競爭激烈，本公司在全球市場中與這些產品的競爭對手競爭。
原料、物料、勞動力、公用設施或服務成本的變動可能大幅提高本公司的營運成本。本公司目前正經歷原料及其他成本的通貨膨脹。本公司已透過調整部分銷售價格，將通貨膨脹的影響轉嫁給客戶，進而部分抵消對利潤的影響。若本公司購入的材料、物料、勞動力、公用設施或服務成本大幅上升，也可能大幅提高本公司的營運成本，若本公司無法將這些成本轉嫁給客戶，可能對本公司業務與營運結果造成重大不利影響。

本公司製造航空複合材料與複合結構及組裝所使用的主導材料，合格供應商數量有限。本公司已為許多，但非全部，原料尋找合格的替代供應來源，但某些原料僅由單一供應商生產。在某些情況下，某些原料的替代品未必總是容易取得，過去也曾出現這些材料市場短缺的情況。某些與飛機相關產品的原料替代可能需要政府（例如 FAA）批准。雖然本公司認為與供應商的關係強，但若這些材料短缺或因天然災害或其他原因導致供應中斷，可能大幅提高本公司的營運成本，並對本公司業務與營運結果造成重大不利影響。同樣地，若本公司購入的材料成本大幅上升，也可能大幅提高本公司的營運成本，若本公司無法將這些成本轉嫁給客戶，可能對本公司業務與營運結果造成重大不利影響。若本公司一個或多個供應商需暫時關閉製造設施，本公司取得製造所需原料的能力可能受到限制，這最終可能限制本公司製造產品的能力。
